bull_bear.body: Geopolitical conflicts, supply chain disruptions, inflationary pressures
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: The company has a strong focus on innovation, with new business wins in double clutches, FEAD timing kits, and bearings
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Working capital is the current call on capital — it rose to 20,291 mn INR (about 19.7% of sales) driven mainly by inventories, and management states levels will be brought back in check in coming quarters.
- Investment is being funded while cash generation is compressed: free cash flow was 2,335 mn INR for 6M 2026 versus 5,239 mn INR a year earlier, squeezed by higher working capital and lower earnings rather than by higher capex.
- The stated philosophy in the closing message is a commitment to deliver results and drive long-term stakeholder value; the deck does not lay out a dividend or buyback policy.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Diversified portfolio across Automotive Technologies, Vehicle Lifetime Solutions and Bearings & Industrial Solutions creates structural balance and resilience through demand cycles
- Access to Schaeffler Group's global engineering expertise, technology platforms and motion-technology heritage (80+ years)
- Deep localisation strategy strengthening supply-chain resilience and competitiveness
- State-of-the-art manufacturing facilities with robust quality systems and process excellence
- Extensive distribution reach: 33,000+ retail network and 330 distribution/channel partners, reinforced by KOOVERS digital aftermarket platform
- Combination of mechanical engineering with electronics/software capability supporting electrified and connected motion systems
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Climate transition and physical climate risk to cost base and supply chain — The BRSR material-issues table flags emissions management as a risk: carbon pricing mandates and regulatory compliance raise operational costs, and policy direction toward low-carbon manufacturing 'may necessitate capital investments and operational changes'. Physically, storms, floods and heatwaves 'could have significant direct and indirect impact on our supply chain and operations, potentially disrupting production and affecting our ability to fulfill demand'. The Company also states it depends on suppliers, primarily in the steel sector, to develop lower-carbon alternatives to control the carbon footprint embedded in its products - i.e. a cost driver it does not control. All manufacturing sites have undergone structured climate risk assessments and climate considerations are embedded into capital expenditure decisions.
- Product quality, safety and regulatory non-compliance risk in OEM supply — Schaeffler India sells into automotive and industrial customers that demand high standards of quality, safety, regulatory compliance and environmental performance; the AR states product quality and safety 'are critical to maintaining customer trust and long-term OEM relationships'. Disclosed downside is recalls, warranty claims, safety incidents, regulatory penalties and reputational damage, mitigated through group-wide product validation and approval processes and a 'zero-defect' culture. The same row concedes incremental capex and opex on R&D and design is required to stay compliant with evolving material-compliance, hazardous-substance and end-of-life requirements.
- Occupational safety exposure across shop floor and contract workforce — Listed in the BRSR table as a pure Risk. Manufacturing operations 'involve significant engagement of employees and contract workers on the shop floor'; lapses could cause injuries, downtime and non-financial impacts 'that are not easily reversible'. Financial exposure named: medical expenses, compensation payments, regulatory penalties, litigation costs, higher insurance premiums and production downtime. The Company notes the nature of operations limits exposure to highly hazardous substances, so the exposure is accident/continuity-driven rather than process-chemical.
- Cyber and data-security risk across ERP, order management and customer engineering data — Listed as a pure Risk. Increasing digitalisation of enterprise systems - specifically ERP, order management and customer-specific engineering data - means a breach could expose sensitive commercial, technical or personal information, disrupt operations, breach data-protection regulation and 'impact long-term customer trust and OEM relationships'. Mitigation is an IT governance framework supported by Group-wide information security (the disclosure is cut off mid-sentence in the routed text), so the control environment is inherited from the parent rather than standalone.
- Input price volatility, import dependence and supplier capacity constraints — The procurement disclosure states localisation 'is at the heart of our strategy' precisely to 'reduce dependence on imports, enhance supply reliability, and respond swiftly to customers', and that the dual-sourcing approach and long-term agreements 'help mitigate risks from price volatility, capacity constraints, and external disruptions'. That is an explicit admission of three live structural exposures - imported input dependence, raw-material/component price volatility, and supplier capacity - in a business whose procurement framework must simultaneously balance cost efficiency against quality, supply consistency and ESG qualification. Sustainable sourcing is reported at 60%.
- Dependence on the Schaeffler Group parent for technology, validation and shared frameworks — Product development is explicitly 'aligned with Schaeffler Group's global R&D agenda', product approval runs through 'group-wide product validation and approval processes', and information security is Group-wide - so the India entity's innovation pipeline and key control frameworks are set outside it. The AR also records that following the Group's merger with Vitesco Technologies the SBTi-validated climate targets 'are currently under review', showing India-level commitments can be reset by parent-level corporate action. Reporting scope reinforces the dependence: performance data relate to Schaeffler India Limited, with Group references included only 'for strategic context'.
- Concentrated board control by parent nominees alongside heavy directorship churn — The 2025 at a Glance governance panel discloses only 38% Independent Directors. During 2025-early 2026 the AR records repeated turnover at committee level: Amit Kalyani resigned from the Board and ceased as NRC Chairperson effective July 23, 2025; Dharmesh Arora ceased as NRC member effective May 31, 2025; Andreas Schick ceased from both the Audit Committee and the Risk Management Committee effective February 24, 2026. Chairmanship of the Risk Management Committee passed from Harsha Kadam to Maximilian Andreas Fiedler, a Non-Executive Non-Independent (parent-nominee) director, effective February 7, 2026 - placing oversight of the enterprise risk framework with a non-independent director.

business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Revenue is spread across three roughly balanced pillars plus exports: Automotive Technologies 35% of Q2 2026 sales, Bearings & Industrial Solutions 35%, Vehicle Lifetime Solutions 12% and Intercompany Exports & others 17% — a mix that blends OEM, aftermarket and industrial cycles.
- The company is embedded in the Schaeffler AG global network, with exports mainly to group companies, giving it a captive channel alongside its domestic OEM and aftermarket business.
- Deep, quality-led OEM entrenchment is evidenced by the Q2 award slate: zero-PPM and Best Value Creation awards from Denso India, Zero PPM and Supplier of the Year (runner-up) from Toyota Kirloskar Auto Parts, Hall of Fame from John Deere, Best Partner 2025 from Voith Turbo and a Special Support award from Escorts Kubota.
- End-market exposure spans passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, tractors, two/three wheelers and core industrial sectors (cement, steel, coal, electricity), which the deck tracks explicitly as its demand drivers.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Subsidiary] KRSV Innovative Auto Solutions Private Limited is a loss-making consolidation drag — on 791 mn INR of Q2 2026 revenue it posted a -17.3% EBITDA and -19.1% EBIT margin, pulling consolidated EBITDA margin to 18.5% from 19.1% standalone.
- [Cost headwind] Management attributes the marginal decline in earnings quality to geopolitical developments, specifically fuel prices and a depreciating INR, rather than to pricing or mix.
- [CSR] The company was recognised in the Tribal and Indigenous Communities Development category at the CSR Convention and Best Practices in CSR Awards 2026, indicating community-development programmes as its main disclosed CSR thrust.
- [Sourcing] Sandvik Mining and Rock Technology India recognised the company with an Agile, Customer-Focused Cost Excellence and Efficient Sourcing award, the deck's only signal on cost and sourcing capability.

business.body: Schaeffler India, part of the Schaeffler Group with over 80 years of motion-technology heritage, designs and manufactures precision-engineered components and system solutions spanning automotive and industrial applications. Its portfolio blends mechanical engineering with electronics and software across Automotive Technologies (E-Mobility, Powertrain and Chassis), Vehicle Lifetime Solutions (aftermarket repair and service), and Bearings & Industrial Solutions (rolling and plain bearings, linear and direct-drive technologies).
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Automotive Technologies:** Hybrid, fully electric and fuel-cell mobility solutions, E-axle systems, Passenger vehicle clutches, Dual mass flywheels
- **Vehicle Lifetime Solutions:** Clutch, engine, transmission and chassis repair solutions, Wipers, Steering & suspension components, Automotive lube vending machines, KOOVERS aftermarket digital platform
- **Bearings & Industrial Solutions:** Rolling and plain bearings (compact high-speed to large-scale), Linear and direct-drive technologies, Deep Groove Ball Bearings, Needle Roller Bearings, Lift mast rollers, Maintenance and monitoring services

outlook.title: Guidance / outlook

outlook.body:
- Cross-architecture capability in Automotive Technologies enables customers to transition at their own pace across 48-volt hybrids, full hybrids, range extenders and fully battery-electric vehicles rather than reacting to a single technology substitution.
- Strengthened R&D through integration of advanced testing, validation, design and prototyping functions to enable faster innovation cycles and better customer alignment.
- Deep localisation strategy: partnering with customers and suppliers early in design and engineering to co-create products for local market needs, and expanding localised production capabilities for hybrid components and electric drives.
- KOOVERS aftermarket expansion: setting up dark stores and hubs nationwide for faster customer access, widening reach and market penetration in the automotive aftermarket.
- Vehicle Lifetime Solutions strategy guided by four interlinked priorities: portfolio expansion, e-commerce, brand visibility and training.
- Progressive Dividend Distribution Policy intending to sustain or raise the dividend each year in conjunction with financial performance and free cash profit generation.
- Progressive Dividend Distribution Policy intending to sustain or raise the dividend each year in conjunction with financial performance and free cash profit generation, formulated under SEBI Regulation 43A (applicable to the company as a top-500 listed entity by market capitalisation, effective July 8, 2016). The Board has approved a target dividend payout ratio of 30% to 50% of annual standalone profit after tax, subject to applicable rules and the Dividend Distribution Policy.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Schaeffler India expanded its manufacturing footprint to five plants during the year with the inauguration of its fifth facility at Shoolagiri, Tamil Nadu (commenced August 2025), dedicated to powertrain and chassis components supporting both conventional and electrified technologies. At the Talegaon (Pune) plant, the Company inaugurated an e-axle production line, marking a structural shift from component manufacturing to system-level EV drive solutions. At the Savli plant, the Company localised steering races manufacturing for two-wheeler EVs and launched three series of Large Steering Race Bearings (SRB) localisation, including the first-time local development of a Large Case Steel Bearing Housing. Overall capex for the year totalled `3,836 million (4.1% of sales), guided by a capital-efficiency framework under which every investment is evaluated on localisation impact, technology relevance and asset turnover, with capital projects rigorously evaluated, approved and monitored, aimed at expanding the business while improving Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) over time.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Automotive Technologies demand supported by recent GST reforms and record festive sales, reflecting robust consumer demand and a recovering market, against ongoing challenges from rare earth materials controls, tariff-driven demand uncertainty and persistent semiconductor shortages.
- GST reforms have stimulated demand growth in passenger vehicles, MHCVs and tractors.
- India's automotive aftermarket (Vehicle Lifetime Solutions) remains structurally attractive, supported by a large and ageing vehicle parc, high vehicle utilisation across segments, strong demand for cost-efficient maintenance solutions, and increasing formalisation of distribution channels.
- India's vehicle parc continues to expand structurally across passenger vehicles, tractors and commercial vehicles; aftermarket ecosystem is formalising and digital channels are gaining relevance.
- India's GDP growth outlook for FY2025-26 revised upward by RBI to 7.3% (from 6.8%), driven by robust domestic demand, income tax and GST rationalisation, softer crude oil prices, and front-loaded government capital expenditure.
- India surpassed Japan in 2025 to become the world's fourth-largest economy (GDP USD 4.18 trillion) and is on a path to become the third-largest economy by 2030 (projected GDP USD 7.3 trillion), supporting a strategic landscape for localised manufacturing and industrial innovation.
- Global growth estimated at 2.7% in 2025 with IMF projecting 3.3% for 2026, aided by technology investment, fiscal/monetary support and easing financial conditions, though global trade outlook remains dampened by tariff-policy uncertainty.
- Nomination by a global original equipment manufacturer of transmission components to meet global and domestic requirements, reinforcing Schaeffler India's role as a strategic global hub for ICE powertrain components.
- Business wins for engine cam phasing systems supporting a key customer's ICE powertrain strategy focused on regulatory compliance and fuel efficiency.
- Capitalised on emerging CAFE norms by delivering tailored solutions to help customers comply with upcoming emission regulations across PV and CV segments.

deepdive.thesis: Schaeffler India Limited is a leading manufacturer of automotive and industrial components, with a strong focus on innovation, sustainability, and customer satisfaction. The company has sustained double-digit growth momentum in Automotive Technologies, Vehicle Lifetime Solutions, and Exports. With a commitment to delivering results and driving long-term stakeholder value, Schaeffler India Limited is well-positioned for future growth.

sk.overview: The DRHP frames Dhoot Transmission within India's automotive Electrical and Electronics (E&E) components industry, principally the wiring harness segment for two-wheelers (2W), three-wheelers (3W) and commercial vehicles (CV), alongside adjacent sensors/controllers, automotive switches and power supply cords. This sits within the broader Indian automotive industry (2W/3W/PV/CV/off-highway), which grew from 21.6 million units (FY20) to 28.2 million units (FY26) at a 4.6% CAGR and is projected to reach 35-45 million units by FY31 (6-8% CAGR). meta.thesis: Schaeffler India Limited is a leading manufacturer of automotive and industrial components, with a strong focus on innovation, sustainability, and customer satisfaction. The company has sustained double-digit growth momentum in Automotive Technologies, Vehicle Lifetime Solutions, and Exports. With a commitment to delivering results and driving long-term stakeholder value, Schaeffler India Limited is well-positioned for future growth.
